children: , the global payments network, pushed deeper into agentic commerce as Alchemy turned its agent-payment framework into a live developer product called AgentCard. Shares were nearly flat at $566.285 Friday morning.

AgentCard gives AI software agents single-use Mastercard credentials tied to a customer's existing account rather than handing a bot permanent access to a payment card. Developers can set spending caps, limit eligible merchants and restrict transactions geographically, while users keep their existing rewards and credit arrangements. Alchemy says the service is already available, giving developers a practical way to let autonomous agents buy goods anywhere Mastercard is accepted online.

The bigger opportunity is straightforward: Mastercard could sit underneath a new layer of AI-driven commerce without needing to build the shopping agents itself. AgentCard tackles the trust problem first by tightly controlling what an AI agent can spend, although neither company has disclosed pricing, transaction volumes or committed customers yet. The valuation picture adds another wrinkle: the chart puts Mastercard at $566.285 versus a GF Value estimate of $683, leaving the shares 17.09% below that benchmark. For investors, the technology is moving from concept to infrastructure; the next test is whether real transaction volume follows.

title: Mastercard Holds Flat as Alchemy Gives AI Agents Spending Controls
